messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a **step‑by‑step guide** for creating a RESTful API request to the *“Get information of device connector versions”* endpoint on **Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1**. I’ll cover both the **web‑UI (API Explorer)** and a **command‑line (curl/Postman)** approach, including authentication, request construction, and how to interpret the response. > **TL;DR** > 1. Log in → Settings → API → Generate a bearer token. > 2. Use the token in a `GET https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions`. > 3. (Optional) Use the built‑in API Explorer to test and copy the request. --- ## 1. Prerequisites | Item | What you need | How to get it | |------|---------------|---------------| | **Dashboard URL** | `https://` | From your network admin or the browser address bar. | | **Admin credentials** | Username & password | Provided by your Nexus Dashboard administrator. | | **API access enabled** | Yes | Verify under *Settings → API* that “Enable API” is checked. | > **Tip:** If you’re unsure of the exact endpoint, you can always look it up in the **API Explorer** (see §2). --- ## 2. Using the Built‑In API Explorer (Web UI) 1. **Log in** to the Nexus Dashboard. 2. Click the **gear icon** (⚙️) → **API** → **API Explorer**. 3. In the left pane, locate the **“Device Connector Versions”** group. 4. Expand it and click **“Get Device Connector Versions”**. 5. The right pane will show the request details: | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | **Method** | `GET` | | **Endpoint** | `/api/v1/device-connector-versions` | | **Query Params** | None (or `limit`, `offset`, `filter` if you want to narrow results) | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer ` (auto‑filled once you log in) | 6. Click **Execute**. 7. The **Response** tab will display the JSON payload and HTTP status code. 8. You can copy the request (method, URL, headers, body) by clicking **Copy** → **cURL** or **Postman**. > **Why use the Explorer?** > • It automatically injects your session token. > • It shows you the exact query parameters and pagination options. > • You can test different filters without writing code. --- ## 3. Manual Authentication & Request (curl / Postman) ### 3.1. Obtain a Bearer Token ```bash # Replace , , curl -k -X POST "https:///api/v1/auth/token" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"username":"","password":""}' ``` **Response** ```json { "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...", "expires_in": 3600, "token_type": "Bearer" } ``` > **Note:** > * `-k` skips certificate verification (use only in dev/test). > * Store the `access_token` securely; it’s valid for 1 hour by default. ### 3.2. Call the Device Connector Versions API ```bash curl -k -X GET "https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` #### Optional Query Parameters | Parameter | Description | Example | |-----------|-------------|---------| | `limit` | Max number of items per page | `limit=200` | | `offset` | Pagination offset | `offset=200` | | `filter` | Simple filter (e.g., `name==v1.2.3`) | `filter=name==v1.2.3` | **Full example with pagination** ```bash curl -k -X GET "https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions?limit=200&offset=0" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` ### 3.3. Sample Response ```json { "total": 3, "limit": 200, "offset": 0, "results": [ { "id": "dcv-001", "name": "v1.0.0", "release_date": "2023-01-15", "description": "Initial release", "status": "stable" }, { "id": "dcv-002", "name": "v1.1.0", "release_date": "2023-04-20", "description": "Bug fixes and performance improvements", "status": "stable" }, { "id": "dcv-003", "name": "v1.2.0", "release_date": "2023-07-10", "description": "New features added", "status": "beta" } ] } ``` > **Pagination** – If `total > limit`, repeat the request with `offset=limit`, `offset=2*limit`, etc., until you’ve retrieved all items. --- ## 4. Common Pitfalls & Troubleshooting | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | `401 Unauthorized` | Token expired or missing | Re‑authenticate or add `Authorization` header | | `403 Forbidden` | User lacks API permissions | Ask admin to grant “API Access” role | | `404 Not Found` | Wrong endpoint or version mismatch | Verify endpoint path (`/api/v1/device-connector-versions`) | | `500 Internal Server Error` | Dashboard bug | Check logs or contact Cisco support | --- ## 5. Quick Reference Cheat Sheet | Step | Command / Action | |------|------------------| | **Login & Get Token** | `curl -X POST https:///api/v1/auth/token -d '{"username":"","password":"

"}'` | | **Call API** | `curl -X GET https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions -H "Authorization: Bearer "` | | **Filter by name** | `.../device-connector-versions?filter=name==v1.2.0` | | **Pagination** | `.../device-connector-versions?limit=100&offset=200` | | **Use Postman** | Import the URL, set `Authorization` → `Bearer Token`, paste token. | --- ## 6. Need the Exact URL? If you’re unsure of the base URL or the exact endpoint path, you can: 1. **Check the API Explorer** (as described in §2). 2. **Ask your Nexus Dashboard admin** for the “API Base URL” (often `https:///api/v1`). 3. **Look at the network traffic** in your browser’s dev tools while clicking the API button; the request URL will be visible. --- ### Final Note The **“Get information of device connector versions”** API is read‑only (`GET`) and does not require a request body. All you need is a valid bearer token and the correct endpoint. Happy querying!
